quests.passage: At the outdoor market, it's normal to haggle over the price of almost everything for sale.
quests.question: to argue back and forth over a price before agreeing on one
quests.hint: Think about what shoppers and sellers do before settling on a final price at this kind of market.
quests.explanation: 'Haggle' means going back and forth with a seller until you agree on a lower price. Doing this for 'almost everything' shows it's an expected part of shopping at this market.
quests.wordInContext: He haggled the vendor down from thirty dollars to twenty for the leather belt.

quests.passage: The store offered a full refund since the jacket still had its original tags attached.
quests.question: money given back to a customer after a purchase is returned
quests.hint: Notice what condition made the store willing to give the money back.
quests.explanation: 'Refund' means the money returned to a customer, usually when an item is brought back. The store agreeing to return it in full, because the tags were untouched, shows this repayment.
quests.wordInContext: She asked for a refund after the shoes fell apart within a week.

quests.passage: Luckily, the blender came with a two-year warranty, so the repair was completely free.
quests.question: a company's written promise to fix or replace a product if it breaks
quests.hint: Think about why the repair didn't cost anything, even though the blender broke.
quests.explanation: 'Warranty' describes a seller's promise to fix or replace a product within a set time if something goes wrong. The free repair, thanks to the two-year coverage, is the warranty in action.
quests.wordInContext: The laptop's warranty expired just one month before the screen cracked.

quests.passage: Buying a new television at midnight was an impulsive decision he regretted by morning.
quests.question: done suddenly, based on a feeling rather than careful thought
quests.hint: Notice the unusual timing of the purchase and how he felt about it just hours later.
quests.explanation: 'Impulsive' describes acting on a sudden urge without thinking it through. A midnight purchase followed by regret by morning is a textbook impulsive decision.
quests.wordInContext: Her impulsive habit of buying shoes online whenever she felt stressed was starting to worry her.

quests.passage: Everything in the clearance section was priced to sell before the new collection arrived.
quests.question: an area or sale where items are marked down to be sold quickly
quests.hint: Think about why the store wants these particular items gone before something else shows up.
quests.explanation: 'Clearance' describes items discounted to sell fast, usually to make space for new stock. Pricing things to move before the new collection arrives is exactly what a clearance sale does.
quests.wordInContext: She found a winter coat for half price in the clearance rack.

quests.passage: The souvenir shop's markup on bottled water was almost triple what it cost at the supermarket.
quests.question: the amount added to a product's cost to set its selling price
quests.hint: Compare what the shop charges to what the same item costs elsewhere.
quests.explanation: 'Markup' describes the extra amount added on top of an item's original cost. Charging triple the supermarket price shows a large markup on this bottled water.
quests.wordInContext: Restaurants often apply a heavy markup on bottled wine compared to what it costs in stores.

quests.passage: The chef added a garnish of fresh mint leaves to brighten up the plate.
quests.question: a small decorative addition to food, meant to improve its appearance
quests.hint: Think about why the chef added these mint leaves — for taste, or for how the plate looks?
quests.explanation: 'Garnish' describes something added to a dish mainly to make it look more appealing. Mint leaves used to 'brighten up the plate' fits this decorative purpose exactly.
quests.wordInContext: A single slice of lemon served as the garnish on top of the grilled salmon.

quests.passage: She let the chicken marinate overnight in garlic, lime, and spices before grilling it.
quests.question: to let food sit in a flavorful liquid before cooking, so it absorbs the flavor
quests.hint: Notice how long the chicken sits in this mixture before it's actually cooked.
quests.explanation: 'Marinate' means soaking food in a seasoned liquid to add flavor before cooking. Leaving the chicken in garlic, lime, and spices overnight gives the flavors time to soak in.
quests.wordInContext: He marinated the tofu for an hour in soy sauce and ginger before frying it.

quests.passage: The recipe called for just five basic ingredients, and every ingredient was already sitting in the pantry.
quests.question: one of the individual foods or substances used to make a dish
quests.hint: Think about what these five items actually are, based on where most of them were found.
quests.explanation: 'Ingredient' describes one of the separate items combined to make a dish. Needing only five, already sitting in the pantry, shows how simple this recipe's ingredient list is.
quests.wordInContext: Flour, sugar, and eggs were the only ingredients the cake required.

quests.passage: Each portion at the restaurant was so large that most customers left with leftovers.
quests.question: the amount of food served to one person at a meal
quests.hint: Think about why so many customers weren't able to finish their plates.
quests.explanation: 'Portion' describes the amount of food given in a single serving. Servings large enough to send most customers home with leftovers shows unusually generous portions.
quests.wordInContext: The nutritionist recommended cutting his dinner portion in half.

quests.passage: After the flu, her mother made a nourishing soup full of vegetables and broth.
quests.question: providing the body with what it needs to recover and stay healthy
quests.hint: Notice why this particular soup was chosen for someone who had just been sick.
quests.explanation: 'Nourishing' describes food that supports the body's health and recovery, often chosen with care for someone who needs it. Making it specifically after the flu shows this healing intent, beyond just being tasty.
quests.wordInContext: The hospital served light, nourishing meals to patients recovering from surgery.

quests.passage: Rice is a staple in many households, appearing at nearly every dinner table.
quests.question: a basic food or item used regularly as part of daily life
quests.hint: Think about how often this food shows up in people's meals, according to the passage.
quests.explanation: 'Staple' describes something used so regularly it becomes a basic, expected part of daily life. Rice appearing at nearly every dinner shows it has become exactly this kind of essential food.
quests.wordInContext: Bread has been a staple of the local diet for generations.

quests.passage: The company decided to upgrade every employee's laptop after years of slow performance.
quests.question: to replace something with a newer or better version
quests.hint: Notice what problem, lasting for years, finally led to this decision.
quests.explanation: 'Upgrade' means replacing something with a newer, improved version. Swapping out laptops after years of slowness is a direct response solved by upgrading.
quests.wordInContext: She decided to upgrade her phone plan after running out of data every single month.

quests.passage: The IT team traced the slow computers to malware hidden inside a downloaded file.
quests.question: harmful software designed to damage or disrupt a computer
quests.hint: Think about what the IT team found buried inside that download, and what it was doing to the computers.
quests.explanation: 'Malware' describes software built to cause harm, often hidden where users won't notice it. Being the hidden cause of the slow computers shows exactly this damaging effect.
quests.wordInContext: The email attachment secretly installed malware that stole passwords from the browser.

quests.passage: The bank's app is built to encrypt every message so that no one else can read your account details.
quests.question: to convert information into a code so only authorized people can read it
quests.hint: Notice what the app is protecting your messages from, and how.
quests.explanation: 'Encrypt' means scrambling information into a code that only the right person can unlock. Making sure no one else can read your account details is exactly what encryption accomplishes.
quests.wordInContext: Companies encrypt customer data before storing it on their servers.

quests.passage: A firmware update fixed the camera's autofocus problem without needing any new hardware.
quests.question: the built-in software that controls how a device's hardware operates
quests.hint: Notice that the fix came through software, not by replacing any physical part.
quests.explanation: 'Firmware' describes the permanent software built into a device that controls how its hardware runs. Fixing the autofocus without new hardware shows the problem lived in this built-in software.
quests.wordInContext: The router needed a firmware update before it would support the faster internet speed.

quests.passage: Streaming video in high quality uses far more bandwidth than sending a simple email.
quests.question: the amount of data that can be sent through an internet connection at once
quests.hint: Compare the two activities mentioned and think about which one needs more capacity to move data.
quests.explanation: 'Bandwidth' describes how much data a connection can handle at a time. High-quality video needing far more of this than a simple email shows the difference in data demand.
quests.wordInContext: The office upgraded its internet plan for more bandwidth once video calls became a daily habit.

quests.passage: The app's new interface made it far easier to find settings that used to be buried in menus.
quests.question: the way a user sees and interacts with a program or device
quests.hint: Think about what part of the app actually changed — not what it does, but how it looks and feels to use.
quests.explanation: 'Interface' describes the visual layout a person uses to interact with software. Settings becoming easier to find, without the app's function changing, points to an improved interface.
quests.wordInContext: The redesigned interface confused longtime users at first, since every button had moved.

quests.passage: Stress at work left him with insomnia, lying awake for hours most nights.
quests.question: difficulty falling or staying asleep
quests.hint: Notice what he's doing instead of sleeping, night after night.
quests.explanation: 'Insomnia' describes an ongoing struggle to fall or stay asleep. Lying awake for hours most nights, caused by work stress, is a clear description of insomnia.
quests.wordInContext: Her insomnia got worse the week before every big exam.

quests.passage: Leafy greens contain iron, a nutrient the body needs to repair itself and grow.
quests.question: a substance in food that the body needs to function and stay healthy
quests.hint: Think about what specifically the body gets from these greens, beyond just calories.
quests.explanation: 'Nutrient' describes a substance in food the body relies on to function and repair itself. Leafy greens being 'packed' with these substances shows their nutritional value.
quests.wordInContext: Vitamin C is a nutrient the body can't produce on its own.

quests.passage: Most days, the clinic treats nothing more serious than a common ailment, like a cold or a mild allergy.
quests.question: a minor illness or health problem
quests.hint: Notice the examples given — colds, sprains, allergies — and what they have in common.
quests.explanation: 'Ailment' describes a health problem, usually not serious. Colds, sprains, and mild allergies are all listed as examples of these everyday ailments.
quests.wordInContext: The pharmacist recommended an over-the-counter remedy for his minor ailment.

quests.passage: After the vaccine, her body became immune to the virus that had spread through the school.
quests.question: protected against a particular disease and unable to be affected by it
quests.hint: Think about what the vaccine changed about her body's ability to catch this virus.
quests.explanation: 'Immune' describes being protected from a disease, usually because the body can now fight it off. Becoming unaffected by the virus that spread through school shows this protection at work.
quests.wordInContext: Once you've had chickenpox, you're usually immune to it for the rest of your life.

quests.passage: The doctor decided to prescribe a short course of antibiotics for the infection.
quests.question: to officially recommend and authorize a specific medicine or treatment
quests.hint: Notice who is making this medical decision and what they're authorizing.
quests.explanation: 'Prescribe' means a doctor officially recommending a treatment or medication. Deciding on a short course of antibiotics is exactly this kind of medical instruction.
quests.wordInContext: The dentist prescribed painkillers for the first few days after the tooth was removed.

quests.passage: He spent two weeks at his parents' house to recuperate fully after the operation.
quests.question: to gradually recover strength and health after an illness or injury
quests.hint: Think about why he chose to stay somewhere else for two full weeks instead of going straight home.
quests.explanation: 'Recuperate' means slowly regaining health and strength after being sick or injured. Spending two weeks focused on recovery after surgery is exactly what recuperating looks like.
quests.wordInContext: The team gave the injured player six weeks to recuperate before returning to matches.

quests.passage: The summer blockbuster earned more in its opening weekend than most films make in a year.
quests.question: a movie that is extremely successful and popular, usually earning huge amounts of money
quests.hint: Notice how the film's opening weekend earnings compare to what most movies make in an entire year.
quests.explanation: 'Blockbuster' describes a film with massive commercial success. Out-earning most movies' full-year total in a single weekend shows the scale of this success.
quests.wordInContext: Studios often release their biggest blockbuster of the year right before summer vacation begins.

quests.passage: Fans had waited three years for the sequel, and it finally answered every question from the first film.
quests.question: a follow-up story or film that continues from an earlier one
quests.hint: Think about how this new film connects to something that came before it.
quests.explanation: 'Sequel' describes a story that continues after an earlier one. Answering questions left open by the first film shows how directly this one picks up where the original left off.
quests.wordInContext: The sequel was released a decade after the first movie, catching up with the same characters as adults.

quests.passage: The director built suspense slowly, letting the music grow tenser before the big reveal.
quests.question: a feeling of tension and anticipation about what will happen next
quests.hint: Notice how the music changes and what that's meant to make the audience feel while waiting.
quests.explanation: 'Suspense' describes the tense, uncertain feeling of waiting to find out what happens. Music growing tenser before the reveal is a technique used specifically to build this anticipation.
quests.wordInContext: The novel kept readers in suspense until the very last page revealed who the culprit was.

quests.passage: The film's climax arrived just as the two rivals finally faced each other on the rooftop.
quests.question: the most intense or important point in a story, usually near the end
quests.hint: Think about where in the story this rooftop confrontation happens, and why it matters so much.
quests.explanation: 'Climax' describes the peak moment of tension or importance in a story. The two rivals finally facing off marks exactly this turning point the whole film has been building toward.
quests.wordInContext: The novel's climax comes when the missing letter is finally discovered in the attic.

quests.passage: The movie's soundtrack became so popular that people streamed it separately from the film itself.
quests.question: the collection of music used throughout a film
quests.hint: Notice that people wanted to listen to this on its own, apart from watching the movie.
quests.explanation: 'Soundtrack' describes the music that accompanies a film. Its popularity growing enough for people to stream it on its own shows how memorable this collection of songs became.
quests.wordInContext: The composer spent eight months writing the film's soundtrack before a single scene was shot.

quests.passage: The season finale ended on such a cliffhanger that fans immediately began guessing what would happen next.
quests.question: an ending left unresolved, creating suspense about what happens afterward
quests.hint: Think about why fans couldn't just relax after watching the finale — what was left unanswered?
quests.explanation: 'Cliffhanger' describes a tense, unresolved ending that leaves the audience wanting more. Fans guessing what comes next right after the finale shows the story was deliberately left hanging.
quests.wordInContext: The book ended on such a cliffhanger that readers demanded the sequel be released early.
